reason: The text contains multiple named characters who are regular people, most notably the widow woman (אִשָּׁה אַלְמָנָה) of Zarephath, who is identified and described as a regular person (not royalty, not a prophet). She serves as a key character in the narrative, along with her son. Additionally, Obadiah (עֹבַדְיָהוּ) is a named character who, while serving in the king's household, is essentially a regular person and not of royal status. Both are clearly distinguished from the prophets (Elijah), kings (Ahab), and other figures of authority in the text.
